title: A penalized spline is a linear mixed model
title_html: A penalized spline is a linear mixed model
html:
Let P be nonnegative definite of order m and rank r=m−k, write P=LL⊤ with L of size m×r and full column rank, let Xγ be m×k with columns spanning N(P), and set Zγ=L(L⊤L)−1.

  1. (The transformation.) [Xγ,Zγ] is nonsingular, so every 𝛄γ is uniquely 𝛄𝛃γ=Xγβ+Zγu; moreover 𝛄u=L⊤γ and 𝛄𝛄γ⊤Pγ=u⊤u.

  2. (The mixed model.) With X=BXγ and Z=BZγ, the P-spline criterion @eq-smo-pspline is 𝛃‖y−Xβ−Zu‖2+λu⊤u,{#eq-smo-mixed}

    which is the penalized criterion @eq-mix-penalized of the linear mixed model 𝛃𝛆Y=Xβ+Zu+ε, u∼Nr(0,σu2I), 𝛆ε∼Nn(0,σ2I) independent, with λ=σ2/σu2.{#eq-smo-lambda-ratio}

    Its solution is Henderson’s (@thm-mix-henderson): 𝛃β^ is the generalized least squares estimate and u^ the BLUP (@thm-mix-blup).

  3. (The Bayesian reading.) Suppose σ2 is known and 𝛄γ has the prior with density proportional to 𝛄𝛄exp⁡{−γ⊤Pγ/(2τ2)}, τ2=σ2/λ — equivalently 𝛃β flat and u∼Nr(0,τ2I). Then 𝛄𝛄γ∣Y=y ∼ Nm{γ^, σ2(B⊤B+λP)−1},{#eq-smo-posterior}

    with 𝛄γ^ the penalized estimate of @prp-smo-pspline-ridge(a).

  4. (REML.) The marginal distribution is 𝛃Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2Vλ) with Vλ=I+λ−1ZZ⊤. Profiling σ2 out of the restricted likelihood (@def-mix-reml, @thm-mix-reml) leaves −2ℓR(λ)=(n−k)log⁡σ^λ2+log⁡|Vλ|+log⁡|X⊤Vλ−1X|+c,{#eq-smo-reml}

    where σ^λ2=y⊤Aλy/(n−k) with Aλ=Vλ−1−Vλ−1X(X⊤Vλ−1X)−1X⊤Vλ−1, and c does not depend on λ. Minimizing @eq-smo-reml over λ>0 estimates the smoothing parameter.
